issues.description: The problem statement's UML and text specify calculateTotalPrice(Meal) should return a double (double precision), but the solution implementation declares calculateTotalPrice as returning an int. This mismatch between the specified return type (double) and the implemented return type (int) can confuse students about the expected method signature and numerical precision to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent. Either change the specification to expect an int (if integer pricing is intended) or update the implementation to return a double. Recommended fix: change the method signature in SealSaloon to public static double calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal) and compute the sum using double (e.g., double sum = 0.0; sum += ingredient.getPrice();), preserving the UML/text expectation of double precision.
